not: A ceremony framework: every mechanism must prevent a real failure worth its cost.
A second source of truth beside Git.
An engine that invents human decisions or acts without authority.
A deploy, CI or release-publishing tool: its release support is a branching strategy.
Inherently opinionated: it ships an opinionated default graph, but every opinion (graph, lenses, prompts, policy) can be customised by the project.
principles: Git is the store; state is visible and repairable by hand.
A small engine; the graph, prompts and policy belong to the project.
Human authority is explicit: approvals may be delegated, but decisions with big consequences go to the owner, batched.
Reviews are independent, and a finding must matter.

Guard against drift at both levels: from what a goal asked for, and from the project's original intent. A goal that departs from the project's intent is flagged when it is added, and the owner either changes the goal or amends the intent.
Prefer deleting to adding; keep prompts distilled.

spec:
Write and maintain docs/WHITEPAPER.md as a long-form, linkable, print-friendly working whitepaper about ZzzOps, linked from README. The owner wants enough precise detail to inspect exactly how the system behaves, spot flaws and keep the document current while the system is refined. Define deterministic progressive disclosure through the actual frontier and per-node task-card mechanism. Preserve prior WD1-WD7 owner decisions: practitioner-first with a technical back half, the deterministic progressive disclosure term, repository Markdown paper plus an owner-published external blog draft, David Rzepa byline with agent drafting/review disclosure, and brief generic related work without benchmarks. WD8 remains applicable if any performance or cost evidence is mentioned: ratios/trends only, with honest sources and caveats. Performance/evaluation material is not required and unsupported claims of reliability, efficiency or causal improvement must be omitted or clearly identified as design aims.

Describe the checked implementation precisely: durable Git data and CAS writes; snapshots and identity rules; leases and actor/independence limits; declarative graphs and configurable prompts/policy; node states and transition triggers; dependency/discovery scheduling; disclosure and actual output-size behavior; findings, filters, corrections, disputes and budgets; approvals, held work and owner questions; code-tree/change fingerprints, staleness, frozen tests, merge sync and carry; stacked PR delivery; Git-flow release/hotfix lines and publication evidence; bootstrap, capability/default-policy adoption; interruption, offline behavior, conflicts and recovery. Distinguish engine enforcement, shipped defaults, root/human procedures and unknowns. Use readable diagrams/tables, concrete worked examples or a clearly synthetic executable trace, an auditable source/test claim ledger, known limits/open audit questions and a short upkeep procedure. The existing SPEC remains the exact schema/algorithm reference. Do not modify the engine or policy/templates to make the document true; record discovered mismatches explicitly and separately.

Bind the paper to explicit checked source and package build, and say which material is implementation, configurable convention or a proposed/unmerged extension. Latest tested/installed development snapshot at preparation is 4ff4e3f188f613adbd22a0726c1bbde69eed9d1b, build 0.0.0-dev a81bbe0dd4ce; integration dev is c455b09914b49fd65e169f91a4f79110e3e2540b. Refresh these facts before writing. Source-backed explanations may include the installed release-summary extension, but must disclose that it is not yet merged into dev. No external publication system, telemetry, benchmark framework or permanent CI guard is required.

Owner clarification supersedes the earlier G1037 merged-report prerequisite: dogfooding was a readiness check to uncover major design changes before drafting, not evidence that the paper must include. Do not wait for, write, incorporate or complete a dogfood report or empirical evaluation as part of this whitepaper goal. Do not claim the old run or any release/deployment succeeded, and do not publish private project identifiers or transcripts. The newer thread offered by the owner is not needed as a paper source.

Owner's purpose, verbatim: "My hope is that if there's enough detail describing exactly the behavior, then I can use it to spot flaws and we can keep it as a working document while we tweak things".
Owner's clarification, verbatim: "We don't need to include dogfood evidence in the paper, I just wanted to finish dogfooding first to ensure there were no major issues that would require changes to the whitepaper".

Migrated from GitHub issue #490 after reset #740; replaces G1002. Preserve existing design/review history and refresh the design through the ordinary goal workflow to reflect this clarified deliverable.
